channel.title: A House-Shaped House
channel.description: A House-Shaped House follows the nearly five years we spent building Echo Pond, as the soil, the bank, the budget, and the ledge kept complicating the project. Life became white-knuckle exciting. It explores the work of building together and whether the people building Echo Pond could survive what construction would ask of them.

item.title: Prologue: The House That Looks Inevitable
item.itunes:title: Prologue: The House That Looks Inevitable
item.description: Beneath the finished image, people were joking, worrying, getting it wrong, and choosing to stay. That’s what makes life so exciting, right?

item.itunes:title: Part I: Before a House Could Be Drawn
item.description: We owned the parcel. We did not know whether it could support a house. After a stalled architectural start, a civil engineer marked a place on an oversized topographic map: here.

item.title: Interlude: What the Echo Returns
item.itunes:title: Interlude: What the Echo Returns
item.description: York Pond located a body of water. Glen Echo presented a destination. Through myth and Thoreau’s woods, an echo becomes more than repetition under constraint.

item.title: Part II: Choosing the House-Shaped House
item.itunes:title: Part II: Choosing the House-Shaped House
item.description: We have to keep it simple. Then the simplest design came in at more than twice our ceiling. Alison wrote five possible futures. One design at one price had failed. The project had not.

item.title: Part III: Paying for the Line on the Drawing
item.itunes:title: Part III: Paying for the Line on the Drawing
item.description: The bank would not pay for dirt, so we committed our own money with no way to know exactly how the rock would break. There’s a lot to absorb here.

item.description: A frost-protected slab, a wire in the middle of nowhere, and the controversial megashingle. You had us at witchy.

item.title: Part V: After Completion Changes Tense
item.itunes:title: Part V: After Completion Changes Tense
item.description: Life had begun. Over coffee, Vincent talked about minimalism, fancy minimalism, and the way people live. But there was still the small matter of the certificate of occupancy.

item.title: Coda: What Returned Changed
item.itunes:title: Coda: What Returned Changed
item.description: The house we had imagined gave way to the house we had always wanted without knowing how to imagine it. Other people’s knowledge had become part of what we loved. So had the people.
